issue_context.title: Combination of groupby with dropna set to True and apply function not returning expected output
issue_context.body:
(Using pandas 1.3.1 and numpy 1.20.3)

This is a repetition of the SO question found [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/68918019/pandas-groupby-with-dropna-set-to-true/68918101?noredirect=1#comment121798992_68918101). (I did not have this issue previously when working with version 1.1.3).

In the following snippet:
```
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "a": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9], 
        "b": [1, np.nan, 1, np.nan, 2, 1, 2, np.nan, 1]
    }
)
df_again = df.groupby("b", dropna=False).apply(lambda x: x)
```
I was expecting df and df_again to be identical. But they are not:
```
df
   a    b
0  1  1.0
1  2  NaN
2  3  1.0
3  4  NaN
4  5  2.0
5  6  1.0
6  7  2.0
7  8  NaN
8  9  1.0

df_again
   a    b
0  1  1.0
2  3  1.0
4  5  2.0
5  6  1.0
6  7  2.0
8  9  1.0
```

Now, if I tweak slightly the lambda expression slightly to "see" what is going on by `df.groupby("b", dropna=False).apply(lambda x: print(x))` I can actually visualize that also the portion of the `df` where `b` was `NaN` was processed.

review_comments: does _selected_obj vs _obj_with_exclusions make a difference here?
no, I think here both would be same
are you suggesting to change this to `_obj_with_exclusions`?

i dont have any reason to think it makes a difference, but big-picture ive been trying to figure out why we use _selected_obj in some places and _obj_with_exclusions in others so we can either a) document the difference and be consistent about it or b) get rid of one of them.

nothing to worry about for this PR, but if you're doing more work in the groupby code, id appreciate extra eyeballs trying to sort this out

The only difference I know is that much of the time, selected_obj includes the grouping column(s) whereas obj_with_exclusions does not. This is not true if a selection is performed after the groupby:

df = pd.DataFrame({'a': [1], 'b': [2], 'c': [3]})
print(df.groupby('a')._selected_obj)   # columns a, b, c
print(df.groupby('a')._obj_with_exclusions)  # columns b, c
print(df.groupby('a')['b']._selected_obj)  # Column b as a Series
print(df.groupby('a')['b']._obj_with_exclusions)  # Column b as a Series
Filter will contain the grouping column, so we need to use _selected_obj here I believe.
